brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Palace Constructor" where users build spatial memory aids by arranging abstract geometric rooms that represent different categories of information they want to memorize, with each room having walls that can be "painted" with mnemonic imagery using a unique interaction where dragging concepts from a central well causes the walls to ripple and absorb the information as living murals that slowly animate and evolve based on how often the user revisits them, requirin
critique: The interface suffers from severe visual incoherence with garish color choices (#f39, #f9c on dark background), inconsistent typography scales, and a cluttered spatial hierarchy that fights against its ambitious memory palace concept. The drag-drop implementation is incomplete, motion animations lack purpose beyond decoration, and the overall execution feels like a rough prototype rather than a thoughtfully crafted experience.
fixes: Replace the jarring neon color palette with a sophisticated monochromatic scheme using subtle gradients and opacity variations to create depth and hierarchy
Implement proper typography system with clear size/weight relationships and remove the awkward text truncation on walls in favor of intelligent labeling
Complete the drag-drop interaction with visual feedback states and redesign the concept well as floating cards with proper shadows instead of the cramped bottom bar
